reviews.decision_reason: synthesize_recommendation deterministically reflects the first row it receives, but the first row is already wrong because prioritize_needs put direct, low-demand evidence ahead of unsupported high-demand evidence. The resulting recommendation is therefore behaviorally wrong: it reports maintain/top_need preserve immutable review attempts even though the highest-ranked observed need is unsupported.

map_coverage preserves all eight handed-off records and marks exact need-to-capability matches as direct while leaving unmatched records unsupported. The output keeps the missing capability for n06-r01 and n06-r07 visible instead of hiding or inventing support.

prioritize_needs reverses the intended demand/frontier ordering by sorting direct coverage before unsupported needs and by treating larger provenance_rank values as higher priority. This pushes unsupported high-demand n06-r01 to priority 8 and low-demand direct n06-r08 to priority 1, contradicting the supplied demand/provenance ranking and causing the downstream maintain recommendation.
